chapter: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
title: Booking out from the Grand Terrace and the first theater tours
summary: Fox booked the band for months on the road; first theater was the Stanley in Pittsburgh.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: That was a darn good band. You didn't work at the Grand Terrace all year round, did you?

No, after we started broadcasting, then, he started booking us out. We'd work sometimes about two or three months at the Terrace, and then go out two or three months and then come back in. In and out, in and out. Most of the time we'd leave after New Year's Eve. And go out and stay three, four months, and then come back in the spring.
You said "they would book." Would Fox book the bands?
Yeah. He didn't trust the different bookers, you know, like William Morris, and oh, different booking agents.
It was easy to book the band then, because we was broadcasting every night.
Right. And you'd get nationally known.
Were they one nighters that you played, or did you have some --
The first time we went out it was a theater engagement.

I think that was at the Stanley Theater in Pittsburgh. And we played one night, I think. Then we came back to the Grand Terrace. Then the next time we went out -- theaters for three weeks. With a few one-nighters, you know, on the way there and on the way back. Then it started getting longer and longer.
More and more one-nighters. More theaters.
What were some of the places that you went?
Well, Dreamland in New York, Savoy
Ballroom in New York. And the rest of the places I can't remember too well. Strand Ballroom in Philadelphia.
